question.text: What will be the maximum intraday value of the VIX over these biweekly periods in Q4 2026? (Nov 9 - Nov 20)
question.resolution_criteria: Each subquestion will resolve as the maximum intraday value of the VIX recorded from the market open on the first Monday to the market close on the last Friday of the specified biweekly period. Specifically, it will resolve as the highest HIGH value for the relevant days in the CSV published [on the Cboe website](https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/vix/vix_historical_data/).
question.fine_print:
* If the market is closed on one or more trading days within the period, only the available trading days will be considered.
* If the resolution source delays or ceases its reporting of these data, Metaculus might use alternative [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) to resolve this question.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left:** The window opens Nov 9, one week from now, and the outcome is known at the close on Nov 20, 2026. That is about 18 days away and covers 10 trading days.

**(b) Latest resolution-source value:** The Cboe CSV shows Oct 30, 2026 with a high of 23.93 and a close of 19.42. Spot on Nov 2 is about 19.1 to 19.9.

**(c) If nothing changed:** If the VIX holds near 19.5, normal intraday excursions over 10 days would put the maximum high around 21 to 22.

**(d) If the current trend continued:** Spikes have been rising, while closes have stayed in the high teens:
- The last four two-week maxima were 18.9, 17.6, 22.3 and 23.9.
- Continuing that pattern points to a maximum of about 22 to 25.
- Against that, mid-November seasonality and post-election relief usually pull volatility down.

**(e) Historical variation:**
- The code baseline for the close 12 days ahead has a median of 19.9, with a 10th percentile of 15.8 and a 90th of 25.0.
- The maximum of daily highs over 10 days sits well above a single close, usually by 1.5 to 3 points above the starting level.
- It also has a fat right tail when a spike happens: recent spike days added 4 to 6 points intraday.

**(f) Experts and markets:**
- There is no direct VIX market for this window.
- Kalshi's Fear & Greed market leans toward "Fear" for Nov 13.
- The WTI market gives meaningful odds of oil above $110.
- CNBC and Nomura describe muted hedging demand and say the VIX is reacting less than usual to selloffs.
- Seasonality generally favors a calmer November.
- Two events fall inside the window: October CPI around Nov 10 to 12, and Nvidia earnings around Nov 18 to 19.

**(g) Scenarios:**
- **Low:** A smooth midterm result, a benign jobs report and a cool CPI print bring a relief rally. The VIX settles near 15 to 16, and the maximum high comes in around 16 to 17.
- **High:** An oil shock above $120 coincides with an AI-trade unwind triggered by Nvidia's reaction and further de-grossing by long-short funds. The VIX gaps up into the 30s, possibly approaching 40 intraday.
